# What Methods are Automatically Generated for a Record?

---

## 🟢 Junior Level

When you declare a `record`, the Java compiler automatically synthesizes **5 core constructs**:

```
  ┌───┬──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ # │ Auto-Generated Construct         │ Generated Signature / Behavior                                  │
  ├───┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 1 │ **Canonical Constructor**        │ `public User(String name, int age)`                             │
  │ 2 │ **Public Accessor Methods**      │ `public String name()` and `public int age()` (No `get` prefix) │
  │ 3 │ **Value-Based `equals(Object)`** │ Compares all components for deep equality.                      │
  │ 4 │ **Consistent `hashCode()`**      │ Computes combined hash based on all components.                 │
  │ 5 │ **Descriptive `toString()`**     │ `User[name=Alice, age=30]`                                      │
  └───┴──────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```java
public record User(String name, int age) {}

// Usage of auto-generated methods:
User user = new User("Alice", 30);           // 1. Canonical Constructor
System.out.println(user.name());             // 2. Accessor -> "Alice"
System.out.println(user);                    // 3. toString() -> "User[name=Alice, age=30]"
System.out.println(user.equals(new User("Alice", 30))); // 4. equals() -> true
System.out.println(user.hashCode());         // 5. hashCode() -> matching hash integer
```

---

## 🟡 Middle Level

### The Accessor Naming Convention

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Record accessors **NEVER use the JavaBean `get` or `is` prefix** unless the component name itself includes it:
> - `record User(String name)` ➔ Accessor is `user.name()` (NOT `user.getName()`).
> - `record Task(boolean active)` ➔ Accessor is `task.active()` (NOT `task.isActive()`).
> - `record Task(boolean isActive)` ➔ Accessor is `task.isActive()`.

### Code Equivalent of Generated `equals()`, `hashCode()`, and `toString()`

```java
// Conceptual implementation generated by the Java runtime:
@Override
public boolean equals(Object o) {
    if (this == o) return true;
    if (!(o instanceof User other)) return false;
    return this.age == other.age && Objects.equals(this.name, other.name);
}

@Override
public int hashCode() {
    return Objects.hash(this.name, this.age);
}

@Override
public String toString() {
    return "User[name=" + this.name + ", age=" + this.age + "]";
}
```

---

## 🔴 Senior Level

### The Byte Array `equals()` & `hashCode()` Trap

> [!CAUTION]
> If a record component is an **Array** (e.g. `byte[]` or `String[]`), the auto-generated `equals()` and `hashCode()` perform **identity comparison (`==`)**, NOT content comparison!
>
> Two separate records with identical byte array contents will return **`equals() == false`**!

```java
// ❌ DANGEROUS: Default equals() fails for array contents:
public record SessionToken(String id, byte[] signature) {}

SessionToken token1 = new SessionToken("1", new byte[]{1, 2, 3});
SessionToken token2 = new SessionToken("1", new byte[]{1, 2, 3});

System.out.println(token1.equals(token2)); // 💥 FALSE! (Array reference identity was compared)
```

```java
// 🟢 SENIOR FIX: Override equals(), hashCode(), and toString() for arrays:
public record SessionToken(String id, byte[] signature) {
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (!(o instanceof SessionToken other)) return false;
        return Objects.equals(id, other.id) && Arrays.equals(signature, other.signature);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(id, Arrays.hashCode(signature));
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "SessionToken[id=" + id + ", signature=" + Arrays.toString(signature) + "]";
    }
}
```

### HotSpot JVM Internals: `ObjectMethods` & `invokedynamic`

Unlike traditional compilers that write static bytecode for `equals()`, `javac` emits an `invokedynamic` instruction pointing to the bootstrap method:
`java.lang.runtime.ObjectMethods.bootstrap(MethodHandles.Lookup, String, TypeDescriptor, Class, String, MethodHandle...)`

This defers the exact hashing and equality strategy to runtime method handles, allowing the JVM JIT compiler to optimize struct field comparisons without bytecode bloat.

---

## 🎯 Interview Cheat Sheet

**Must Know:**
- **5 Generated Constructs:** Canonical constructor, accessor methods (no `get`), `equals()`, `hashCode()`, `toString()`.
- **Accessor Naming:** Matches component name exactly (`user.email()`, `user.active()`).
- **Indy Optimization:** `equals()`, `hashCode()`, and `toString()` are linked dynamically via `ObjectMethods.bootstrap`.
- **Array Trap:** Records with array components perform identity `==` checks; you **must** override `equals()` and `hashCode()` using `Arrays.equals()` and `Arrays.hashCode()`.

**Common Follow-up Questions:**
- *"Can you customize or override any of the auto-generated methods?"* → Yes; you can override any accessor, `equals()`, `hashCode()`, `toString()`, or the canonical constructor.
- *"Does a record generate setters?"* → No; records are strictly immutable value carriers.
- *"Does Jackson ObjectMapper work with record accessors without `get`?"* → Yes; modern Jackson (2.12+) supports Java records natively without requiring `@JsonProperty` on accessors.

**Red Flags (DO NOT Say):**
- ❌ *"Records generate `getName()` and `setName()` methods."* (Records generate `name()` and have no setters).
- ❌ *"Records with byte array fields automatically compare array elements in `equals()`."* (They perform pointer comparison `==`; you must override `equals` with `Arrays.equals`).
- ❌ *"You are not allowed to override `toString()` in a record."* (You can freely override `toString()`, `equals()`, and accessors).
